decisions.reason: The firm has sunk visible resources into a dedicated offshore unit and publicly linked it to its strategic expansion, so management is likely to persist with this flagship, core-adjacent service unless failure becomes unmistakable.

This service broadens the firm's maritime support offer with relatively limited additional commitment, and any weaker recent performance can plausibly be blamed on temporary travel disruption rather than a bad strategic fit.

Because the portal was presented as a flagship digital extension of the core service model, management has reputational and sunk-cost reasons to continue backing it despite uncertain evidence on uptake.

The app is less publicly central than the flagship launches and could be consolidated if underused, but its fit with safer and more efficient vessel operations still makes continued commitment more likely than withdrawal.
